original_target.title: Is the extinction-to-propagation threshold sharp for bistable fractional diffusion?

full_original_statement:
On the real line, consider $`u_t+(-\Delta)^\alpha u=f(u)`$ with $`0<\alpha<1`$, where $`f`$ is bistable, for example $`f(u)=r u(u-\theta)(1-u)`$ on $`0<u<1`$, with $`r>0`$ and $`0<\theta<1/2`$. Start from $`u(0,x)=(\theta+\varepsilon)\mathbf 1_{(-L,L)}(x)`$, where $`0<\varepsilon\leq1-\theta`$ and $`L>0`$.

For fixed $`\varepsilon`$, let $`L^{\mathrm{ext}}_\varepsilon`$ be the supremum of lengths for which $`u(t,\cdot)\to0`$ uniformly, and let $`L^{\mathrm{prop}}_\varepsilon`$ be the infimum of lengths for which $`u(t,\cdot)\to1`$ locally uniformly. Under the assumptions of Faye and Zhao, both thresholds are positive and finite. Must

```math
L^{\mathrm{ext}}_\varepsilon=L^{\mathrm{prop}}_\varepsilon
```


hold for every admissible $`\varepsilon`$, at least for the cubic bistable reaction above? This asks whether there is a single critical interval length separating extinction from propagation.

sources.scope_comparison: Publisher Figure1 describes numerically computed equality for selected cubic parameters, not an all-alpha/all-amplitude theorem. Local asks equality of extinction/propagation lengths for each admissible amplitude on R for fractional Laplacian, distinct from bounded convolution dispersal. Current author page links HALv3; HAL denies access with Anubis, publisher full HTML sends no-login page. No complete claim located, but theorem-body comparison remains a source gap; retain partial status without declaring completed scope audit.

rationale: The HALv3 introduction explicitly leaves fractional-Laplacian sharpness open, even for the cubic case. Separate positive finite extinction and propagation thresholds and small-amplitude bounds with logarithmic separation do not establish equality at every amplitude. Numerical Figure1 does not establish the universal assertion.
